description: Train developers on secure code review from vulnerability pattern education through hands-on exercises to reviewer competency assessment.

steps.description: Catalog the vulnerability patterns developers must recognize for the target stack, grouped by weakness class and severity.

inputs.name: tech-stack
inputs.desc: Languages, frameworks, and runtime the team builds on

inputs.name: target-languages
inputs.desc: Primary languages reviewers will read and assess

outputs.name: vulnerability-pattern-library
outputs.desc: Catalog of weakness patterns keyed to language and framework

outputs.name: pattern-severity-map
outputs.desc: Severity and likelihood rating for each cataloged pattern

process: Map the target stack to the weakness classes it is most exposed to
Collect concrete code patterns that express each weakness in the target languages
Rate each pattern by severity, exploitability, and prevalence in the stack
Organize the patterns into a reviewer-facing library with lookup by language

steps.description: Map each vulnerability pattern to the secure coding standard and anti-pattern example that teaches the fix.

inputs.name: vulnerability-pattern-library
inputs.desc: Catalog of weakness patterns from the pattern step

inputs.name: tech-stack
inputs.desc: Languages, frameworks, and runtime the team builds on

outputs.name: secure-coding-standards
outputs.desc: Standard rules that prevent each cataloged pattern

outputs.name: anti-pattern-examples
outputs.desc: Paired vulnerable and fixed code snippets per rule

process: Select the coding standard clause that neutralizes each pattern
Write a vulnerable snippet and its corrected counterpart for each clause
Note the review signal that lets a reader spot the pattern quickly
Record gaps where no standard yet covers a cataloged pattern

steps.description: Design hands-on review exercises built from seeded vulnerable code samples tied to the pattern library.

inputs.name: vulnerability-pattern-library
inputs.desc: Catalog of weakness patterns from the pattern step

inputs.name: secure-coding-standards
inputs.desc: Standard rules that prevent each cataloged pattern

outputs.name: hands-on-exercises
outputs.desc: Review exercises with learning goals and expected findings

outputs.name: vulnerable-code-samples
outputs.desc: Seeded code containing known planted weaknesses

process: Plant a known weakness from the library into a realistic code sample
Define the expected findings and the standard rule each exercise exercises
Grade exercises by difficulty from single obvious flaw to subtle chained flaws
Write an answer key that maps each planted flaw to its fix

steps.description: Build the code review checklist and scoring rubric reviewers apply during live review.

inputs.name: secure-coding-standards
inputs.desc: Standard rules that prevent each cataloged pattern

inputs.name: pattern-severity-map
inputs.desc: Severity and likelihood rating for each cataloged pattern

outputs.name: code-review-checklist
outputs.desc: Ordered checks a reviewer runs against each change

outputs.name: review-rubric
outputs.desc: Scoring rubric for reviewer accuracy and coverage

process: Translate each standard rule into a concrete yes or no review check
Order checks by severity so high-impact weaknesses are caught first
Define rubric levels for finding rate, false positive rate, and depth
Mark which checks a static analyzer can automate versus human-only checks

steps.description: Plan a facilitated review session where developers work the exercises against the checklist.

inputs.name: hands-on-exercises
inputs.desc: Review exercises with learning goals and expected findings

inputs.name: code-review-checklist
inputs.desc: Ordered checks a reviewer runs against each change

outputs.name: session-plan
outputs.desc: Timed agenda pairing exercises with checklist practice

outputs.name: facilitation-guide
outputs.desc: Facilitator notes, prompts, and discussion points

process: Sequence exercises from warm-up to the hardest chained-flaw case
Pair each exercise with the checklist sections it should surface
Write facilitator prompts that steer discussion toward missed findings
Build in a debrief that compares participant findings to the answer key

steps.description: Assess reviewer competency against the rubric and produce a targeted training improvement plan.

inputs.name: review-rubric
inputs.desc: Scoring rubric for reviewer accuracy and coverage

inputs.name: session-plan
inputs.desc: Timed agenda pairing exercises with checklist practice

outputs.name: competency-scorecard
outputs.desc: Per-reviewer scores for finding rate and accuracy

outputs.name: training-improvement-plan
outputs.desc: Follow-up practice targeted at each weak area

process: Score each reviewer against the rubric on finding rate and false positives
Identify weakness classes a reviewer repeatedly misses
Recommend targeted exercises for each identified gap
Set a re-assessment cadence to confirm the gaps close

description: Gather and validate security requirements from abuse case analysis through threat-driven requirements, acceptance criteria, and traceability.

steps.description: Analyze the system context, data sensitivity, and trust boundaries that scope security requirements.

inputs.name: system-description
inputs.desc: What the system does, its users, and its interfaces

inputs.name: data-sensitivity-profile
inputs.desc: Classification of the data the system handles

outputs.name: system-context-model
outputs.desc: Actors, assets, and data flows in scope

outputs.name: trust-boundary-map
outputs.desc: Boundaries where trust level changes across the system

process: List actors, external systems, and the assets each one touches
Trace data flows and mark where data crosses a trust boundary
Classify each asset by sensitivity and regulatory obligation
Record assumptions about the deployment and threat environment

steps.description: Develop abuse cases and misuse scenarios that describe how an attacker subverts each trust boundary.

inputs.name: system-context-model
inputs.desc: Actors, assets, and data flows in scope

inputs.name: trust-boundary-map
inputs.desc: Boundaries where trust level changes across the system

outputs.name: abuse-cases
outputs.desc: Attacker goals framed as negative use cases

outputs.name: misuse-scenarios
outputs.desc: Step-by-step scenarios of abuse across boundaries

process: For each trust boundary, name the attacker goal that violates it
Write the abuse case as a negative counterpart to a normal use case
Describe the misuse scenario as concrete attacker steps
Tag each scenario with the asset and boundary it targets

steps.description: Derive security requirements that counter each abuse case, with rationale tied back to the threat.

inputs.name: abuse-cases
inputs.desc: Attacker goals framed as negative use cases

inputs.name: trust-boundary-map
inputs.desc: Boundaries where trust level changes across the system

outputs.name: security-requirements
outputs.desc: Testable requirements that counter the abuse cases

outputs.name: requirement-rationale
outputs.desc: The threat each requirement answers and why

process: Map each abuse case to the control that would prevent or detect it
State each control as a testable requirement, not an implementation
Record the rationale linking the requirement to its abuse case
Flag abuse cases that no requirement yet addresses

steps.description: Write acceptance criteria and verification methods that make each requirement objectively checkable.

inputs.name: security-requirements
inputs.desc: Testable requirements that counter the abuse cases

inputs.name: misuse-scenarios
inputs.desc: Step-by-step scenarios of abuse across boundaries

outputs.name: acceptance-criteria
outputs.desc: Pass or fail conditions for each requirement

outputs.name: verification-methods
outputs.desc: How each requirement will be tested or reviewed

process: Turn each requirement into observable pass or fail conditions
Choose a verification method of test, review, analysis, or demonstration
Reuse misuse scenarios as negative test conditions
Confirm each criterion is measurable without interpreting intent

steps.description: Prioritize the security requirements by risk reduction and cost so scope decisions are explicit.

inputs.name: security-requirements
inputs.desc: Testable requirements that counter the abuse cases

inputs.name: requirement-rationale
inputs.desc: The threat each requirement answers and why

outputs.name: prioritized-requirements
outputs.desc: Requirements ordered by risk reduction and cost

outputs.name: priority-rationale
outputs.desc: The basis for each priority ranking

process: Score each requirement by the risk it reduces using its rationale
Estimate implementation and verification cost for each requirement
Rank requirements by risk reduction per unit of cost
Document the basis so scope cuts can be defended later

steps.description: Build the traceability matrix linking abuse cases to requirements, criteria, and tests as a baseline.

inputs.name: prioritized-requirements
inputs.desc: Requirements ordered by risk reduction and cost

inputs.name: acceptance-criteria
inputs.desc: Pass or fail conditions for each requirement

outputs.name: traceability-matrix
outputs.desc: Links from abuse case to requirement to criteria to test

outputs.name: requirements-baseline
outputs.desc: Versioned baseline of the agreed requirement set

process: Link each abuse case forward to its requirement and acceptance criteria
Flag any requirement with no criterion or any abuse case with no requirement
Capture the agreed set as a versioned baseline
Define how changes to the baseline will be tracked

description: Design security tests driven by threat models from attack tree analysis through test case generation, automation, and coverage measurement.

steps.description: Ingest the threat model and architecture into a threat inventory and attack surface map for test planning.

inputs.name: threat-model
inputs.desc: Existing threat model with threats and assumptions

inputs.name: system-architecture
inputs.desc: Components, interfaces, and data flows of the system

outputs.name: threat-inventory
outputs.desc: Normalized list of threats with affected assets

outputs.name: attack-surface-map
outputs.desc: Entry points and interfaces exposed to attackers

process: Normalize threats from the model into a consistent inventory
Map each threat to the components and interfaces it targets
Enumerate entry points to form the attack surface map
Flag threats with no corresponding entry point for review

steps.description: Build attack trees that decompose each priority threat into attacker steps and rank the paths.

inputs.name: threat-inventory
inputs.desc: Normalized list of threats with affected assets

inputs.name: attack-surface-map
inputs.desc: Entry points and interfaces exposed to attackers

outputs.name: attack-trees
outputs.desc: Goal-to-step decompositions for each threat

outputs.name: attack-path-rankings
outputs.desc: Paths ranked by feasibility and impact

process: Set each priority threat as the root goal of an attack tree
Decompose the goal into sub-goals and leaf attacker actions
Rank each root-to-leaf path by feasibility and impact
Mark the paths that most warrant dedicated test cases

steps.description: Generate security test cases from the ranked attack paths, including the data each test needs.

inputs.name: attack-trees
inputs.desc: Goal-to-step decompositions for each threat

inputs.name: attack-path-rankings
inputs.desc: Paths ranked by feasibility and impact

outputs.name: test-cases
outputs.desc: Security test cases with preconditions and expected results

outputs.name: test-data-requirements
outputs.desc: Inputs, accounts, and fixtures each test needs

process: Turn each ranked attack path into one or more concrete test cases
Define preconditions, attacker action, and expected secure outcome
List the test data, accounts, and fixtures each case requires
Tag each test case with the threat and path it exercises

steps.description: Turn the automatable test cases into scripts and a harness configuration for repeatable runs.

inputs.name: test-cases
inputs.desc: Security test cases with preconditions and expected results

inputs.name: test-data-requirements
inputs.desc: Inputs, accounts, and fixtures each test needs

outputs.name: automated-test-scripts
outputs.desc: Scripts that run the automatable test cases

outputs.name: test-harness-config
outputs.desc: Environment and fixture setup for the scripts

process: Separate cases suited to automation from those needing manual testing
Script each automatable case with setup, action, and assertion
Configure the harness to provision the required test data
Record which cases remain manual and why

steps.description: Measure how well the test suite covers the attack surface and identify the uncovered gaps.

inputs.name: automated-test-scripts
inputs.desc: Scripts that run the automatable test cases

inputs.name: attack-surface-map
inputs.desc: Entry points and interfaces exposed to attackers

outputs.name: coverage-report
outputs.desc: Coverage of attack surface and threats by the suite

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Entry points and threats with no covering test

process: Map each test back to the entry points and threats it exercises
Compute coverage across the attack surface and threat inventory
List entry points and threats that no test currently covers
Rank the gaps by the impact of the threats they leave untested

steps.description: Plan how the suite is maintained and run as a regression gate as the system and threats change.

inputs.name: coverage-gaps
inputs.desc: Entry points and threats with no covering test

inputs.name: test-cases
inputs.desc: Security test cases with preconditions and expected results

outputs.name: maintenance-plan
outputs.desc: How tests are updated as threats and code change

outputs.name: regression-strategy
outputs.desc: Which tests gate which stages of the pipeline

process: Schedule new test work to close the ranked coverage gaps
Define triggers that require tests to be revisited on change
Select the regression subset that gates each pipeline stage
Set a review cadence to retire stale tests and add new ones

description: Build and operate a fuzz testing harness from target selection through harness writing, corpus management, and crash triage.

steps.description: Select and prioritize fuzz targets from the codebase by input exposure and parsing complexity.

inputs.name: codebase-profile
inputs.desc: Structure, languages, and entry points of the codebase

inputs.name: input-interfaces
inputs.desc: Interfaces that accept external or untrusted input

outputs.name: fuzz-targets
outputs.desc: Functions and parsers selected as fuzz targets

outputs.name: target-prioritization
outputs.desc: Targets ranked by exposure and parsing risk

process: Identify functions that parse or decode untrusted input
Rate each candidate by input exposure and parsing complexity
Select targets with clear input boundaries suited to fuzzing
Rank the selected targets so effort goes to the riskiest first

steps.description: Construct the fuzz harness and instrumentation that feeds inputs to each selected target.

inputs.name: fuzz-targets
inputs.desc: Functions and parsers selected as fuzz targets

inputs.name: input-interfaces
inputs.desc: Interfaces that accept external or untrusted input

outputs.name: harness-code
outputs.desc: Harness entry points that drive each fuzz target

outputs.name: instrumentation-config
outputs.desc: Coverage and sanitizer instrumentation settings

process: Write a harness entry point that maps fuzzer bytes to target inputs
Isolate the target so each run starts from a clean state
Enable coverage feedback and memory or undefined-behavior sanitizers
Verify the harness drives the target before any campaign

steps.description: Build a seed corpus from real inputs and prior cases and measure its baseline coverage.

inputs.name: fuzz-targets
inputs.desc: Functions and parsers selected as fuzz targets

inputs.name: harness-code
inputs.desc: Harness entry points that drive each fuzz target

outputs.name: seed-corpus
outputs.desc: Initial inputs that exercise diverse target paths

outputs.name: corpus-coverage-baseline
outputs.desc: Coverage the seed corpus reaches before fuzzing

process: Collect valid real-world inputs and prior test cases for each target
Add minimal structurally valid inputs where real samples are scarce
Run the corpus through the harness to record baseline coverage
Remove redundant seeds that add no new coverage

steps.description: Run the fuzzing campaign against the harness and collect crashes and coverage over time.

inputs.name: harness-code
inputs.desc: Harness entry points that drive each fuzz target

inputs.name: seed-corpus
inputs.desc: Initial inputs that exercise diverse target paths

outputs.name: campaign-results
outputs.desc: Coverage growth, executions, and timing of the run

outputs.name: crash-artifacts
outputs.desc: Crashing inputs and their reproduction data

process: Start the campaign from the seed corpus with defined time or iteration limits
Track coverage growth and execution rate to judge progress
Save each unique crashing input with its reproduction metadata
Stop when coverage plateaus or the limit is reached

steps.description: Triage crashing inputs into unique root causes and assess their exploitability.

inputs.name: crash-artifacts
inputs.desc: Crashing inputs and their reproduction data

inputs.name: harness-code
inputs.desc: Harness entry points that drive each fuzz target

outputs.name: triaged-crashes
outputs.desc: Crashes deduplicated by root cause with repro steps

outputs.name: exploitability-assessment
outputs.desc: Severity and exploitability rating per root cause

process: Reproduce each crash and deduplicate by stack and faulting condition
Minimize each crashing input to its smallest reproducer
Classify the fault type and assess exploitability and severity
Package each unique crash with repro steps for the owning team

steps.description: Minimize and maintain the corpus so coverage is preserved and future campaigns start strong.

inputs.name: seed-corpus
inputs.desc: Initial inputs that exercise diverse target paths

inputs.name: campaign-results
inputs.desc: Coverage growth, executions, and timing of the run

outputs.name: minimized-corpus
outputs.desc: Smallest corpus that preserves achieved coverage

outputs.name: corpus-maintenance-plan
outputs.desc: How the corpus and harness are kept current

process: Merge campaign-discovered inputs into the working corpus
Minimize the corpus to the smallest set that holds coverage
Store the minimized corpus for reuse as a future seed
Define when to refresh the harness and rerun the campaign

description: Manage dependency vulnerabilities from scanning through prioritization, patching, and tracking across the software portfolio.

steps.description: Scan project manifests across the portfolio to inventory dependencies and their known vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: project-manifests
inputs.desc: Dependency manifests and lockfiles across projects

inputs.name: repository-inventory
inputs.desc: List of repositories and services in the portfolio

outputs.name: dependency-inventory
outputs.desc: Direct and transitive dependencies with versions

outputs.name: vulnerability-findings
outputs.desc: Known vulnerabilities matched to dependency versions

process: Parse manifests and lockfiles to resolve direct and transitive dependencies
Record the exact version and source for each dependency per repository
Match versions against vulnerability advisory data
Capture evidence and advisory identifiers for each finding

steps.description: Correlate findings across projects to group the same vulnerability and the components it affects.

inputs.name: vulnerability-findings
inputs.desc: Known vulnerabilities matched to dependency versions

inputs.name: dependency-inventory
inputs.desc: Direct and transitive dependencies with versions

outputs.name: correlated-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: Findings grouped by advisory across the portfolio

outputs.name: affected-components
outputs.desc: Services and repositories each vulnerability touches

process: Group findings that share an advisory across repositories
Resolve whether each finding is reachable or only transitively present
List every component and service affected by each advisory
Flag duplicate findings that collapse to a single upgrade

steps.description: Prioritize the correlated vulnerabilities by exploitability, reachability, and business exposure.

inputs.name: correlated-vulnerabilities
inputs.desc: Findings grouped by advisory across the portfolio

inputs.name: affected-components
inputs.desc: Services and repositories each vulnerability touches

outputs.name: prioritized-vulnerabilities
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities ordered by urgency to remediate

outputs.name: risk-scores
outputs.desc: Risk score and basis for each vulnerability

process: Score each vulnerability by severity, exploit availability, and reachability
Weight by the exposure of the components it affects
Order the vulnerabilities into a remediation queue
Record the basis for each score so priorities can be defended

steps.description: Plan remediation for the prioritized queue, assessing upgrade impact and safe target versions.

inputs.name: prioritized-vulnerabilities
inputs.desc: Vulnerabilities ordered by urgency to remediate

inputs.name: dependency-inventory
inputs.desc: Direct and transitive dependencies with versions

outputs.name: patch-plan
outputs.desc: Target versions and sequence for each remediation

outputs.name: upgrade-impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Breaking changes and effort for each upgrade

process: Determine the fixed version or mitigation for each vulnerability
Assess breaking changes and effort for each upgrade path
Sequence upgrades to minimize churn and conflicting version pins
Note vulnerabilities with no fix that need a compensating control

steps.description: Validate each patch against tests and prepare rollback procedures before and after rollout.

inputs.name: patch-plan
inputs.desc: Target versions and sequence for each remediation

inputs.name: upgrade-impact-assessment
inputs.desc: Breaking changes and effort for each upgrade

outputs.name: validated-patches
outputs.desc: Patches confirmed against build and test suites

outputs.name: rollback-procedures
outputs.desc: Steps to revert each patch if it regresses

process: Apply each patch in an isolated branch and run the full test suite
Confirm the vulnerability is resolved and no regression is introduced
Document rollback steps and version pins for each change
Stage validated patches for rollout in the planned sequence

steps.description: Track remediation status and trends across the portfolio with metrics and alerting.

inputs.name: validated-patches
inputs.desc: Patches confirmed against build and test suites

inputs.name: risk-scores
inputs.desc: Risk score and basis for each vulnerability

outputs.name: tracking-dashboard
outputs.desc: Status of open and closed vulnerabilities by service

outputs.name: remediation-metrics
outputs.desc: Time to remediate and backlog trend over time

process: Record remediation status for each vulnerability by component
Compute time-to-remediate and open backlog against risk score
Surface overdue high-risk items for escalation
Set alerting thresholds for new findings and aging items
